lens: Layout and typography within the existing compact dark design. All fourteen crops inspected. Responsive/accessibility scores cover visible wrapping, legibility and non-colour cues only; no interaction testing, measured contrast or outer-padding assessment.

findings: Before hierarchy and typography/numbers: regular-weight account names resemble the subordinate quota labels, while bold percentages attract attention first. Increase account-name weight; after implements this fix.
After preserves aligned percentage columns and keeps amber warnings subordinate to the account headings. No score drops.

Before hierarchy and typography/numbers: account names lack a clear weight distinction from warning descriptions. Use heavier account headings; after fixes this without wrapping names or displacing percentages.
The three columns remain readable at this width, with consistent label and value alignment. No score drops.
Before hierarchy and typography/numbers: account headings and their warning lines have similar typographic emphasis. Increase heading weight; after makes each stacked account easier to identify.
After retains visible separators, right-aligned percentages and a header arrangement that accommodates Expand All without overlapping the counts. No score drops.
Before hierarchy: the long account name has the same regular weight as subordinate text. Give the name moderate emphasis; after improves its identification as the account heading.

Both layout scores: the three-line first account name makes that account substantially taller than its neighbours and pushes its warning down. Provide a concise display name for this compact view while retaining the complete credential label in the expanded details.

Typography/numbers drops from 8 to 7: before has a lengthy regular-weight heading; after turns it into a dense three-line bold block beside 82.8%, with more text concentrated in the final line. Use semibold for account names and a concise display name to reduce the visual mass.
The complete label, percentage and unavailable-quota message remain visible; no clipping is apparent.
Before hierarchy and typography/numbers: the amber unavailable message competes with its regular-weight account heading. Increase heading weight; after establishes a clearer parent heading.

Both content scores: '2 loaded · 3 eligible' leaves the counted object implicit despite three visible account rows. Add a noun identifying what loaded, such as 'quota readings', if that matches the intended meaning.
The missing value remains an em dash with an explicit 'Weekly quota unavailable' explanation. No score drops.
Before typography/numbers: regular-weight account names are weaker than the percentages. Increase heading weight; after fixes this.

Both hierarchy and controls/states scores: the stale 82.8% retains the same bold white emphasis as fresh values, while 'Stale' is lighter text immediately beside it. Give the stale qualifier stronger visual grouping, such as a compact outlined badge, and slightly reduce the stale number's emphasis.

Both content scores: '2 loaded' sits above three numeric percentages, leaving the treatment of the stale reading unclear. Label the count's intended category explicitly, such as fresh readings if that is what it counts.
After improves account-heading hierarchy but leaves stale-value emphasis unchanged. The timestamp provides useful visible context. No score drops.

Before hierarchy and typography/numbers: account names do not sufficiently separate from adjacent 'Pro · 100 pts' metadata and subordinate quota labels. Increase account-name weight; after establishes that distinction while preserving numeric alignment.

Before layout and consistency: the lower 'Last observed' and 'Predicted empty' blocks start left of the quota-label alignment above. Align these lower labels and values to the quota text; after implements this consistently across all three accounts.

Both colour scores: progress tracks are very subdued against the dark panel, especially the empty Cloud Session Credits track. Lighten the track colour slightly so its full extent remains easier to perceive without a filled segment.
Both content scores: the standalone 'Current' label does not say what the following percentages represent. Replace it with 'Quota remaining' or an equally explicit label matching the intended metric.
After preserves aligned lower sections and clear warning text. No score drops.
